intro.title: Discover Kupittaa Park
intro.description:
Step into Kupittaa Park and be instantly embraced by the serene Nordic greenery. No commercial bustle, just endless lawns, lush trees, crystal-clear lake waters, and winding paths — every corner radiates natural healing energy.

I visited on a summer morning, sunlight filtering through branches to create dappled patterns, a gentle breeze carrying subtle fragrances of grass, flowers, and greenery. The lawns were vast and soft, the lake calm and clear, waterbirds swimming leisurely, century-old trees standing quietly, telling stories of 170 years.

Park visitors moved at an unhurried pace — joggers on paths, picnickers on lawns, children playing joyfully in Mini-City, their laughter echoing through the gardens. Vintage sculptures and commemorative plaques dotted the landscape, adding profound cultural depth to the natural scenery.

There's no rushing here, only slowing down and finding peace. In the evening, the setting sun bathed the gardens in warm golden hues, the lake sparkled, and tree shadows stretched gently — Kupittaa Park perfectly blends Nordic serenity with urban vibrancy. Healing and beautiful.

sections.title: 170 Years of Royal & Urban History
sections.content:
Kupittaa Park's origins trace back to 1820, initially a promenade beside a spa bathhouse. In 1852, architect Gustav Strengel formally designed and built it, becoming Finland's first planned urban park.

The park's Sacred Spring holds legendary history — it's said that in midsummer 1155, Bishop Henry baptized Finland's first pagans here. In the 18th century, this served as a spa bathhouse, carrying Finnish religious and secular historical memories.

After completion, the park underwent multiple expansions and renovations, adding outdoor pools, children's playgrounds, and sports facilities, gradually developing into an urban green core integrating natural landscapes, historical sites, and recreation.

sections.title: Architecture & Garden Features
sections.content:
Spanning approximately 24 hectares, the park features expansive lawns, formal gardens, winding paths, and lake scenery as its core, complemented by vintage sculptures, commemorative plaques, and century-old trees.

Home to Finland's oldest outdoor swimming pool (built 1912), Mini-City for children, and adventure playground — natural landscapes and recreational facilities blend perfectly. 19th century Nordic Romantic garden style, balancing English landscape natural wildness with French garden formal layouts, featuring smooth flowing lines and rich plant layering.

sections.title: Cultural Significance
sections.content:
Turku's urban green lung, the core gathering place for locals across generations, witnessing Finland's transformation from medieval times to modern era.

The Sacred Spring carries legends of Finland's 1155 baptism, serving as a spiritual symbol of Finnish national culture and representing Nordic outdoor lifestyle aesthetics. For centuries, Kupittaa Park has witnessed Turku's evolution from medieval town to modern city, transforming from exclusive royal noble territory to shared public space — today it remains an irreplaceable spiritual retreat for locals.

sections.title: Outdoor Swimming Pool
sections.content:
Finland's oldest outdoor swimming pool, built in 1912, remains the most popular summer facility. The pool sits adjacent to the lake, allowing swimmers to enjoy lake and mountain views simultaneously.

Open summer (June-August): 09:00-20:00. Admission: Adults €20, Students €15, Children €10. Check daily water temperature forecasts in advance and avoid peak hours.

transport.title: How to Get Here
transport.fromAirportDesc: Take airport bus or tram to city center, transfer to short-route bus directly to park entrance, approximately 25 minutes total. Airport rideshares can reach directly — ideal for luggage and group travel.
transport.fromStationDesc: Take Tram Line 1 or short-route bus, arrive at park area stops within 10 minutes, 3-minute walk to entrance. Public transport runs frequently.
transport.fromOldTownDesc: Walkable from Turku Old Town and Aura River waterfront — city pedestrian paths are well-connected, ideal for hiking串联打卡.
transport.cyclingDesc: Public cycling stations available around the park, suitable for short trips. Park paths are gentle and comfortable for cycling.
transport.dayPassDesc: Purchase Turku public transport day pass for unlimited tram and bus rides, efficiently explore all city attractions.

route.title: Recommended Route
route.overview: Recommended to enter the park in early morning. Start from the main entrance, stroll along the central tree-lined path, visit the Sacred Spring, century-old trees and vintage sculptures, wander through gardens and lakeside, tour Mini-City and outdoor pool, finally relax on the lawn area. The entire route is relaxed — approximately 2 hours for pure sightseeing, half-day for deeper exploration.
steps: Arrive at nearby public transport stop, walk to Kupittaa Park main entrance
Stroll along central tree-lined path, admire expansive lawns and lush tree landscapes
Visit the Sacred Spring area, learn about Finnish religious historical legends and cultural origins
Check in century-old trees and vintage sculptures, observe 19th century garden design details
Wander through garden paths, admire seasonal flower landscapes and horticultural designs
Stroll along lakeside, observe waterbirds and lake scenery up close
Tour Mini-City and adventure playground, experience family recreation atmosphere
Visit outdoor swimming pool area, learn about Finland's oldest pool's history
Relax at expansive lawn area, experience locals' daily picnic and relaxation
Exit through park side gate, connect to nearby Old Town and Aura River attractions

officialManagement.title: About Kupittaa Park
officialManagement.text:
Kupittaa Park is managed and maintained by the City of Turku, and is one of Finland's most important historical and cultural heritage sites.

As Finland's oldest planned urban park, Kupittaa Park has witnessed over 170 years of Turku's urban development. Today, the park is open to the public free of charge, serving as the core recreational space for Turku residents and an important window for visitors from around the world to learn about Finnish history and culture.
